subject: Can I use R-INLA to generate 2D realizations just like sequential Gaussian simulations?

messages.author: 82a29501c95feac5
messages.subject: Can I use R-INLA to generate 2D realizations just like sequential Gaussian simulations?
parts: Hi all, I want to use INLA-SPDE to model my 2D point observations. I want to generate many, say 300, realizations (2D grid) of the potential random field conditioned to the known observations, just like sequential Gaussian simulations in geostatistics. Whether can R-INLA do this? Thank you.

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Can I use R-INLA to generate 2D realizations just like sequential Gaussian simulations?
parts:
On Sun, 2019-08-25 at 01:20 -0700, Jian WANG wrote:
> Hi all, I want to use INLA-SPDE to model my 2D point observations. I
> want to generate many, say 300, realizations (2D grid) of the
> potential random field conditioned to the known observations, just
> like sequential Gaussian simulations in geostatistics. Whether can R-
> INLA do this? Thank you.

yes, inla.posterior.sample, inla.qsample

check the SPDE book at r-inla.org/books



--

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Can I use R-INLA to generate 2D realizations just like sequential Gaussian simulations?
parts:
This function just sample from the internal joint approximation to the posterior distribution, hence is conditioned on the data. 

> n=100
> y=0.1+x+rnorm(n,sd=0.01)
> r=inla(y ~ 1 + x, data=data.frame(y,x), control.compute=list(config=TRUE))
> xx=inla.posterior.sample(10, r)
 round(dig=3,inla.posterior.sample.eval(function() c(Intercept=Intercept, x=x), xx))
          sample:1 sample:2 sample:3 sample:4 sample:5 sample:6 sample:7
Intercept    0.101    0.100      0.1    0.101    0.099      0.1    0.101
x            1.001    0.999      1.0    0.998    1.000      1.0    1.000
          sample:8 sample:9 sample:10
Intercept    0.101      0.1     0.100
x            1.001      1.0     1.001

>
